prize_parts.citation: for the invention and realization of optical lattice clocks, bringing atomic timekeeping to the 10^-18 level

statement.case_for: I opened with B020 first and B030 second, and having read the eight ballots I now put B030 first. Optical lattice clocks are a complete invention-plus-realization story: Katori's magic-wavelength proposal removed Doppler, recoil and lattice light-shift limits, and Ye's group turned it into record accuracy and stability near 1e-18 with many-body interrogation. The idea is original, the result is measurable, independent laboratories in several countries reproduce it, and the impact is concrete: the coming redefinition of the second, relativistic geodesy and sharper tests of fundamental constants. As an experimentalist who builds instruments, I value a prize that rewards an instrument whose performance has been independently verified. The two-name attribution is also the cleanest on the shortlist, and it was supported strongly and from several directions in the opening round: three first places and six top-three rankings, from atomic, theory, statistical and instrument-oriented members.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is overlap with prizes already given. The 2005 prize recognised the optical frequency comb and precision spectroscopy, and the 2012 prize recognised control of single trapped quantum systems, so a committee could see lattice clocks as an incremental extension of recognised metrology. Credit also omits contributors the supplied names do not cover, such as the trapped-ion clock groups and the Lemonde, Lisdat and Ludlow lines. Finally, the formal redefinition of the second is still pending, so the societal payoff is anticipated rather than completed. My own preferred alternative, IceCube (B020), remains the better case if the committee wants a new observational window, and it is the one I would revert to if colleagues judged the attribution gap there smaller than I now do.

responses.point: Danielsson ranked B020 first, naming Halzen and Karle and leaving the third place open, and argued the neutrino flux is a genuine new window that constrains cosmic-ray acceleration, while ranking B017 (Higgs) second.
responses.response: I agree with the science and I opened with B020 for the same reason. But his own hesitation over the third name is what moved me. I proposed Spiering as the third, and Danielsson does not, and neither of us can show from the supplied text how credit divides among conception, construction and analysis across AMANDA and IceCube. That is a larger attribution problem than anything in B030. I also disagree with him on B017: the Higgs discovery is outstanding but five credited names, with ATLAS, CMS and the LHC machine each needing representation, cannot be forced into three people without an arbitrary cut. I would keep B020 as my first alternative, not the preferred prize.

responses.point: Lindroth ranked B030 first, calling it a clear original idea with a measurable payoff, but flagged that the 2005 prize covered the comb and the 2012 prize covered trapped-ion control, and that the redefinition of the second is still pending.
responses.response: I accept her description of the physics and her maturity judgement. I would qualify the overlap point slightly: the 2005 and 2012 prizes honoured enabling tools and single-ion control, whereas the lattice clock's distinct contribution is a many-atom neutral system with the statistics of an ensemble and the accuracy of an ion, which is a different invention. I share her caution that the pending redefinition means the case rests on demonstrated performance, not on a completed adoption, and I would want the citation worded around the invention and its accuracy and not around the redefinition.

responses.point: Kroll ranked B030 first, with Katori's magic-wavelength proposal plus Ye's group's record accuracy and comparison technology as a clean two-person configuration, noting Lemonde and the ion-clock neighbours as other contributors.
responses.response: I agree with his attribution reading and the two-name configuration, and with his emphasis on independent reproduction in national laboratories and on operating clock networks. Where I would press him is on the omitted contributors: Lemonde, Ludlow and others are not a footnote for the committee, and a two-name citation will be criticised for them. I think that is a defensible cost because the conceptual origin (Katori) and the decisive demonstration of ultimate performance (Ye) are identifiable, but he should say plainly that it is a judgement and not a clean fact.

responses.point: Johansson ranked B029 (circuit QED) first as the architectural basis of superconducting quantum processors, while conceding the 2025 prize on neighbouring superconducting-circuit physics may make the committee wait, and that Wallraff is missing from the credit.
responses.response: I take the importance of circuit QED seriously, but I would not put it above B030 now. The missing Wallraff and the five-person 2004 author list make attribution among Schoelkopf, Girvin and Blais harder than the clock case, and the 2025 prize on neighbouring circuit physics makes timing the more delicate. I do not think the practical dominance of the architecture, which is real, substitutes for a clean three-name allocation. Johansson's own timing caveat points the same way.

uncertainties: Whether the committee would treat lattice clocks as distinct enough from the 2005 comb and 2012 trapped-ion prizes.
Whether omitting the trapped-ion clock groups and other lattice-clock contributors such as Lemonde, Lisdat and Ludlow would be judged a serious attribution gap.
For B020, how credit divides among conception, construction and analysis across AMANDA and IceCube, including whether Spiering belongs; I have not independently verified the detailed history.
Whether a prize before the formal redefinition of the second is premature in the eyes of metrology colleagues.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent for B030, and I have no documented tie to Katori or Ye. My astroparticle background and my work on PAMELA, Fermi-LAT, PoGOLite/PoGO+ and XL-Calibur make me close to the field of B020, with no recorded personal tie to its credited names, so I flag the subject proximity to the committee for B020 without claiming a recusal-level conflict.
